variations.name: Battery-electric trains & locomotives
variations.description: Lithium-ion battery packs replace or supplement diesel engines in multiple-unit passenger trains and freight locomotives, charging from overhead wires or regenerative braking to eliminate diesel on non-electrified track at lower infrastructure cost than full electrification.

companies.name: Wabtec
companies.what: FLXdrive heavy-haul battery locomotive (up to ~7 MWh) for freight and mining railroads
companies.signal: Orders from Union Pacific, CN, Rio Tinto, BHP, Roy Hill and Vale; BHP units arrived at Port Hedland Nov 2025

companies.name: Stadler Rail
companies.what: FLIRT Akku battery multiple-unit, the European volume leader for replacing diesel railcars on partially electrified lines
companies.signal: 55 units in service in Schleswig-Holstein and 44 in Rhineland-Palatinate; new orders from ODEG (14) and DB Regio Thuringia (19, service 2028)

companies.name: Siemens Mobility
companies.what: Mireo Plus B battery EMU platform sold across German regional networks
companies.signal: In revenue service in Germany with multiple follow-on fleet orders

companies.name: Progress Rail (Caterpillar)
companies.what: EMD Joule battery-electric switcher and line-haul locomotives
companies.signal: Joule units delivered for long-term demonstration at Pacific Harbor Line, California; battery locomotive momentum building across Class I demos

companies.name: Alstom
companies.what: Coradia battery-electric multiple units (BEMUs) for German regional lines; pivoting rolling-stock R&D from hydrogen to battery
companies.signal: BEMU fleets ordered in Germany while hydrogen train development was paused in 2025

companies.name: Hitachi Rail
companies.what: Battery-hybrid and tri-mode (electric/battery/diesel) intercity trains, including the Trenitalia 'Blues' fleet and UK intercity battery trains
companies.signal: April 2025 UK contract for 45 intercity battery-hybrid cars worth ~£300M including 10-year maintenance

variations.name: Autonomous battery railcars & rail freight innovation
variations.description: Self-propelled, battery-electric railcars that move individually or in small platoons without a locomotive or crew, aiming to win short-haul container and bulk freight back from diesel trucks by making rail economical at small batch sizes.

companies.name: Parallel Systems
companies.what: Autonomous battery-electric intermodal railcars that platoon; second-generation vehicle FRA-approved for pilot on two Genesee & Wyoming short lines in Georgia
companies.signal: $38M Series B extension April 2025 (~$100M total raised); 300+ railcar backlog; commercial launch targeted 2026

companies.name: Intramotev
companies.what: TugVolt self-propelled battery railcars that convert existing freight cars; first mover in revenue industrial service
companies.signal: Autonomous railcars in commercial operation at a Missouri calcium mine; near deal for intermodal cars with an international customer

variations.white_space: Effectively a two-startup US field: FRA certification, railroad operating-rule conservatism, and Class I labor agreements make entry brutal, while the prize (the ~70% of US freight ton-miles on trucks) is huge. Openings exist for European/Asian equivalents on lighter-regulated networks and for retrofit propulsion/automation kits for existing railcar fleets.

variations.name: Hydrogen trains
variations.description: Fuel-cell multiple units and locomotives store compressed hydrogen onboard to replace diesel on long non-electrified routes where batteries lack range, but early fleets have hit reliability and fuel-supply problems and several buyers are reverting to battery trains.

companies.name: Alstom
companies.what: Coradia iLint, the world's first hydrogen passenger train, operating fleets in Lower Saxony and Hesse, Germany
companies.signal: Fleets in service since 2022 but plagued by reliability issues; Alstom paused hydrogen train development in France in 2025 and buyers are shifting future orders to battery

companies.name: Stadler Rail
companies.what: FLIRT H2, the first FRA-compliant hydrogen passenger train in US revenue service (SBCTA Arrow line, Metrolink)
companies.signal: Revenue service since September 2025; Guinness record 2,803 km on one fill; Caltrans ordered six more for 2027 service

companies.name: Siemens Mobility
companies.what: Mireo Plus H hydrogen EMU launched on Berlin's Heidekrautbahn
companies.signal: Entered service December 2024 but was withdrawn within a fortnight over unreliable hydrogen supply — emblematic of fuel-chain risk

companies.name: CRRC
companies.what: Hydrogen fuel-cell switching locomotives and urban trains deployed domestically in China
companies.signal: HFC switcher in service with ~972 km range; multiple Chinese demonstration fleets

companies.name: CPKC (Canadian Pacific Kansas City)
companies.what: Railroad self-developing high-horsepower hydrogen line-haul locomotive conversions using Ballard fuel cells; licensed conversion kit to CSX
companies.signal: Multiple converted locomotives running in Canada; CSX unveiled its first H2 locomotive from the joint program

companies.name: Ballard Power Systems
companies.what: Dominant fuel-cell stack supplier to rail programs (Siemens Mireo Plus H, CPKC, Stadler)
companies.signal: Rail is one of its core verticals; company in deep cost restructuring through 2026 amid slow hydrogen demand

variations.name: Rail electrification & discontinuous catenary technology
variations.description: Overhead catenary electrification is the proven, lowest-emission way to decarbonize heavy rail traffic; the new 'discontinuous' approach wires only sections of a route and lets battery-hybrid trains bridge the gaps, cutting capital cost on bridges, tunnels and rural stretches.

companies.name: Furrer+Frey
companies.what: Swiss overhead-line specialist supplying catenary systems and standardized opportunity-charging stations for battery trains on discontinuous schemes
companies.signal: Its chargers are baseline infrastructure in UK discontinuous electrification planning

companies.name: Hitachi Rail
companies.what: Tri-mode (25kV/battery/diesel) and battery-hybrid intercity trains designed specifically to exploit partial electrification
companies.signal: £300M UK battery-intercity order April 2025; East West Rail's £2.5B 'partial-discontinuous electrification' decision (Nov 2025) validates the model

companies.name: Siemens Mobility
companies.what: Sicat catenary systems plus Mireo Plus B battery trains as the rolling-stock half of discontinuous schemes
companies.signal: Catenary and BEMU products deployed across European networks

companies.name: Alstom
companies.what: Electrification systems including APS ground-level power supply plus BEMU fleets for gap-running
companies.signal: Global electrification and BEMU contracts as 2025 became 'the year of the fleet order' for battery-hybrid trains

companies.name: SPL Powerlines
companies.what: One of the largest overhead-line electrification contractors in the UK and Central Europe
companies.signal: Major framework contractor on UK Network Rail electrification programs

companies.name: Balfour Beatty
companies.what: Civil and rail-systems contractor delivering UK electrification (e.g., TransPennine Route Upgrade)
companies.signal: Long-standing electrification delivery partner on multi-billion-pound UK rail upgrades

variations.name: Locomotive repowering & hybrid retrofits
variations.description: Replacing or augmenting the diesel engines in existing locomotives with hybrid-electric, dual-fuel RNG, or battery modules cuts fuel use 30-50% at roughly half the cost of new locomotives, attacking the long-lived legacy fleet that full replacement can't reach for decades.

companies.name: OptiFuel Systems
companies.what: Modular diesel-RNG dual-fuel hybrid repower packages for line-haul and switcher locomotives, claiming 30-40% fuel reduction with no frame modifications
companies.signal: Argentina repower contract won; 5,000 hp RNG-hybrid line-haul unit testing at TTC Pueblo 2025-26 targeting FRA concurrence 2027

companies.name: ZTR
companies.what: Locomotive modernization, hybrid-electric conversion kits, and fuel-telemetry (Vision) systems
companies.signal: Launched hybrid-electric locomotives with Union Pacific; claims >8,000 gallons of diesel saved per locomotive annually

companies.name: Progress Rail (Caterpillar)
companies.what: EMD modernization and repower programs, including conversions toward Joule battery configurations
companies.signal: Active modernization backlog across Class I and industrial fleets

companies.name: Wabtec
companies.what: Locomotive modernization programs (DC-to-AC conversions) that cut fuel burn across legacy fleets, alongside FLXdrive hybridization
companies.signal: Thousands of modernizations delivered; modernization is a core profit segment

companies.name: First Mode
companies.what: Hybrid hydrogen-battery retrofit powertrains for mining haul trucks and rail
companies.signal: Filed Chapter 11 in December 2024 after Anglo American pulled back; assets and technology portfolio bought by Cummins (announced Feb 2025)

companies.name: Cummins (Accelera)
companies.what: Acquired First Mode's hybrid mining and rail retrofit product lines, folding them into its powertrain decarbonization portfolio
companies.signal: First Mode asset acquisition closed 2025; rail/mining hybrid retrofits now an incumbent-owned line

variations.white_space: Thin field for zero-emission repowers: railroads sweat 30+ year assets and CARB's in-use locomotive rule was withdrawn from EPA waiver consideration in early 2025, gutting the regulatory driver. An opening exists for financing-wrapped repower-as-a-service priced against fuel savings rather than emissions mandates.

variations.name: Fuel cell systems for road vehicles & material handling
variations.description: PEM fuel-cell stacks convert hydrogen to electricity onboard; the technology is commercially proven in forklifts (fast refueling for 24/7 warehouses, ~70k units deployed) and buses, but on-road truck demand stalled in 2024-25, triggering a brutal supplier shakeout.

companies.name: Plug Power
companies.what: GenDrive forklift fuel cells (Amazon, Walmart) plus electrolyzers and hydrogen plants — the largest material-handling fuel cell installed base
companies.signal: Closed $1.66B DOE loan guarantee Jan 2025 then suspended loan-program activities Nov 2025; CEO transition and first-ever positive gross margin reported March 2026

companies.name: Ballard Power Systems
companies.what: Heavy-duty PEM stacks powering buses (Wrightbus, Solaris, New Flyer), rail and trucks
companies.signal: Multi-phase restructuring with full opex-reduction benefit expected in 2026 amid slower-than-expected hydrogen adoption

companies.name: PowerCell Group
companies.what: Swedish fuel-cell stacks and systems for vehicles, marine and stationary power, spun out of Volvo
companies.signal: Niche commercial revenues across marine/vehicle segments; one of few European pure-plays still independent

companies.name: Cellcentric
companies.what: Daimler Truck-Volvo 50/50 JV building truck fuel-cell systems for the Mercedes GenH2 program
companies.signal: Powers GenH2 customer-trial fleet; large-series gigafactory plans slowed as truck FCEV timelines slipped

companies.name: Symbio
companies.what: French fuel-cell maker (Forvia/Michelin/Stellantis JV) with a gigafactory in Lyon
companies.signal: Stellantis abandoned hydrogen and exited July 2025, removing ~80% of planned volumes; Michelin/Forvia warned of 'irreversible consequences' and took 50/50 ownership by May 2026

companies.name: Accelera by Cummins
companies.what: Fuel-cell power systems and electrolyzers within Cummins' zero-emissions division; absorbed First Mode's technology
companies.signal: Diversified incumbent able to outlast pure-plays; First Mode assets acquired 2025

companies.name: Nuvera Fuel Cells (Hyster-Yale)
companies.what: Fuel-cell engines for forklifts and heavy equipment under Hyster-Yale
companies.signal: Hyster-Yale's April 2025 strategic realignment drastically downsized the fuel-cell program, concluding it would not reach profitability in acceptable time ($15-18M severance/impairment)

companies.name: Toyota
companies.what: Third-generation fuel-cell system supplier (co-developed with BMW for the 2028 iX5) and fuel-cell modules for trucks and forklift partners
companies.signal: Gen-3 FC system 25% smaller, launching with BMW's 2028 series FCEV

variations.name: Hydrogen & H2-ICE trucks
variations.description: Heavy trucks powered either by fuel cells or by modified hydrogen-combustion diesel engines promise diesel-like range and refueling times without tailpipe CO2, but three of the most prominent startups went bankrupt in 2024-25 as fuel cost and station scarcity crushed economics.

companies.name: Hyundai Motor
companies.what: XCIENT Fuel Cell, the only series-produced FCEV heavy truck, deployed in 10 countries
companies.signal: ~10M cumulative miles; 30 trucks at Ports of Oakland/Richmond (largest North American H2 truck deployment) and 21 at Georgia Metaplant; new XCIENT unveiled at ACT Expo 2025

companies.name: Daimler Truck
companies.what: Mercedes-Benz GenH2 liquid-hydrogen fuel-cell truck
companies.signal: Second-phase customer trials with five logistics partners; series production pushed toward late decade

companies.name: Nikola
companies.what: US fuel-cell Class 8 truck maker and HYLA fueling brand
companies.signal: Filed Chapter 11 February 2025 with >$1B liabilities after battery recall and cash burn; workforce wound down to one employee

companies.name: Hyzon Motors
companies.what: Fuel-cell truck upfitter spun out of Horizon Fuel Cell
companies.signal: Announced liquidation December 2024 after weak sales and SEC settlement; final asset sale approved 2025

companies.name: Quantron
companies.what: German hydrogen and electric truck converter/OEM
companies.signal: Declared insolvency in late 2024 — one of three H2 truck startups to fail within six months

companies.name: Hyroad Energy
companies.what: Texas company that bought 113 Nikola FCEVs plus all Nikola IP out of bankruptcy to relaunch hydrogen trucking with fuel service
companies.signal: Acquired Nikola trucks/IP for $3.85M (assets valued >$100M), court-approved August 2025; positioning as post-Nikola H2 trucking leader

companies.name: MAN Truck & Bus
companies.what: hTGX hydrogen-combustion (H2-ICE) truck for niche heavy-haul duties, alongside a battery-first strategy
companies.signal: ~200-unit small series delivering from 2025 to Germany, Netherlands, Norway, Iceland; 56 kg at 700 bar, ~600 km range

companies.name: JCB
companies.what: Purpose-built hydrogen combustion engines for construction machines and gensets
companies.signal: H2 engine achieved EU Stage V certification, approved in 10+ European countries with NOx ~98% below limits

companies.name: KEYOU
companies.what: Munich startup converting existing diesel truck engines to hydrogen combustion (~80% of engine unchanged), sold as pay-per-use 'H2-Mobility-as-a-Service'
companies.signal: First converted 18t trucks delivered to pioneer customers from early 2025 (EP-Trans); Komatsu dump-truck conversion proof-of-concept

companies.name: Hydra Energy
companies.what: Canadian hydrogen-diesel co-combustion retrofits (reversible kit, up to ~40% emission cut) paired with its own fueling in BC's Prince George trucking corridor
companies.signal: 300,000+ km of on-road fleet testing; hydrogen-as-a-service contracts with commercial fleets

variations.name: Hydrogen refueling networks & onboard storage tanks
variations.description: High-pressure (350/700 bar), liquid, and cryo-compressed storage tanks plus public refueling stations are the enabling infrastructure for all hydrogen transport; light-duty networks are shrinking (Shell exited California) while investment shifts to heavy-duty corridors and higher-density tank formats.

companies.name: FirstElement Fuel
companies.what: Operates the True Zero network, the world's largest retail hydrogen station footprint (~40 stations in California), expanding into heavy-duty truck fueling
companies.signal: 41st station opened in Oakland; backed by Air Liquide, Mitsui and Japanese OEMs

companies.name: OneH2
companies.what: Modular hydrogen production and portable/turnkey fueling systems delivered to fleet sites, bypassing big-station capex
companies.signal: Investment from Chevron, Trafigura and The Papé Group; supplying 24/7 truck station tech in California

companies.name: Shell
companies.what: Former light-duty hydrogen retail pioneer whose retreat defines the segment's struggles
companies.signal: Permanently closed all seven California light-duty H2 stations in Feb 2024 and canceled 48 planned stations, citing supply complications

companies.name: H2 Mobility
companies.what: Operator of Germany's national hydrogen station network (~90 stations), refocusing from cars to heavy-duty trucks and buses
companies.signal: Largest European HRS network; shareholder base includes Air Liquide, Linde, Daimler Truck, Shell and Hy24

companies.name: Air Liquide
companies.what: Industrial-gas major building hydrogen stations, liquefaction and heavy-duty corridor JVs (TEAL Mobility with TotalEnergies)
companies.signal: Global station portfolio plus investor in FirstElement Fuel

companies.name: Nikola (HYLA fueling)
companies.what: Planned national HYLA truck-fueling network that died with the parent company
companies.signal: Never-installed stationary HYLA refueling equipment (valued ~$14M) was excluded from the Hyroad bankruptcy purchase; mobile fuelers dispersed

companies.name: Hexagon Purus
companies.what: Leading Type IV composite hydrogen cylinder and vehicle-systems maker (transit bus, truck, distribution modules)
companies.signal: Supplied New Flyer five consecutive years, but FY2025 revenue fell 39%; ~30% workforce cut and NOK 350M cost program amid hydrogen slowdown

companies.name: NPROXX
companies.what: Type IV high-pressure hydrogen tanks for vehicles and transport, run as a 50/50 JV with Cummins
companies.signal: Named alongside Hexagon Purus as a leading European H2 tank player; Cummins co-ownership secures OEM channel

companies.name: Verne
companies.what: San Francisco startup commercializing cryo-compressed hydrogen (CcH2) storage claiming 33% more density than liquid H2 and 87% more than 700-bar gas
companies.signal: Demonstrated its first CcH2 truck in Southern California in late 2024; backed by Amazon's Climate Pledge Fund and DOE awards

companies.name: Cryomotive
companies.what: German developer of cryogenic compressed hydrogen storage and refueling hardware targeting diesel-parity range for long-haul trucks
companies.signal: CcH2 tank/refueling platform in truck demonstrations with partners since 2024

variations.name: E-fuels & low-carbon road fuels (e-gasoline, e-diesel, rDME)
variations.description: Synthetic drop-in fuels made from green hydrogen and captured CO2 (or renewable DME from waste) can decarbonize existing combustion fleets without new vehicles or infrastructure, but cost 3-6x fossil fuel today, confining road use to racing, classics and regulatory niches.

companies.name: HIF Global
companies.what: Operates the Haru Oni e-gasoline plant in Chile (with Porsche offtake) and is developing the world's largest e-fuels facility in Matagorda, Texas
companies.signal: Only operating commercial e-gasoline producer; first US CARB LCFS Tier II design pathway for e-fuels (March 2025); Texas project permitted with 1.8 GW electrolysis

companies.name: Infinium
companies.what: Electrofuels producer whose Pathfinder plant (Corpus Christi) supplies e-diesel to Amazon trucking; building the larger Project Roadrunner in West Texas
companies.signal: Roadrunner FID/construction 2025 with Brookfield and Breakthrough Energy Catalyst backing and HSBC project financing; 23,000 t/yr from 2027

companies.name: P1 Fuels
companies.what: Berlin maker of 100% fossil-free drop-in gasoline used in FIA rally/racing series, pushing toward road-fuel mass market
companies.signal: Demonstration plant opened in Germany 2024; raising for industrial-scale plant (~2029)

companies.name: Zero Petroleum
companies.what: UK synthetic-fuels company (Paddy Lowe) with proprietary DirectFT process making petrol, diesel and jet from air-captured CO2 and water
companies.signal: $36M raised; Plant Zero.1 near Oxford running, commercial-scale plant targeted for 2026 production; PwC Net Zero Future50 2025

companies.name: Oberon Fuels
companies.what: Produces renewable dimethyl ether (rDME) from waste/biogas as a diesel substitute, propane blend, and hydrogen carrier
companies.signal: First commercial rDME facility (Brawley, CA); EPA RFS pathway approved; WEF Technology Pioneer 2025; DOE-funded rDME-to-hydrogen project with Los Alamos

companies.name: Porsche
companies.what: Automaker anchor investor in HIF Global, using Haru Oni e-fuel in motorsport and dealer fueling to keep combustion models viable
companies.signal: ~$75M+ invested in HIF; e-fuel used in Porsche Supercup and experience centers

variations.white_space: Few players because green-H2 + DAC economics put e-gasoline at multiples of fossil prices, and most e-fuel capital is being diverted to aviation where SAF mandates guarantee demand. The EU's 2035 e-fuels carve-out for combustion cars creates a future certified e-gasoline supply-chain niche (certification, blending, distribution) that is nearly empty today.

variations.name: Freight logistics optimization & intermodal shift software
variations.description: Software that pools partial truckloads, optimizes routing, and gives shippers real-time multimodal visibility cuts empty miles and enables shifting freight from road to rail — decarbonization through utilization rather than new hardware.

companies.name: project44
companies.what: End-to-end multimodal shipment visibility platform (ocean, rail, road) used for emissions tracking and modal decisions
companies.signal: Unicorn valued ~$2.7B (2022); weathered freight-recession workforce cuts and remains category leader

companies.name: Flock Freight
companies.what: Shared-truckload brokerage that algorithmically pools partial shipments into one truck, eliminating LTL cross-docking and empty space
companies.signal: $60M Series E (May 2025) led by O'Neil Strategic Capital; AI engine evaluates trillions of freight combinations; largest STL broker in US

companies.name: Loadsmart
companies.what: AI-driven freight pricing, instant booking and dock scheduling; strategic investors include CSX and Maersk, linking it to intermodal shift
companies.signal: Raised $200M+ to date; expanded into logistics AI tooling through the freight downturn

companies.name: Convoy
companies.what: Digital freight network that promised to eliminate the ~35% of miles trucks drive empty
companies.signal: Raised ~$900M (peak $3.8B valuation) then shut down October 2023; tech sold to Flexport for ~$16M, and Convoy Platform resold to DAT for $250M in July 2025

companies.name: FourKites
companies.what: Real-time supply-chain visibility platform competing with project44 across modes
companies.signal: Survived FreightTech downturn restructurings; large enterprise shipper base

companies.name: DAT Freight & Analytics
companies.what: Dominant US loadboard/marketplace incumbent that absorbed Convoy's matching and drop-trailer technology
companies.signal: Bought the Convoy Platform from Flexport for $250M (July 2025), consolidating digital freight matching

companies.name: Uber Freight
companies.what: Digital brokerage and managed-transportation arm of Uber optimizing network utilization at scale
companies.signal: Multi-billion-dollar revenue run-rate; survived sector shakeout that killed Convoy

variations.white_space: General freight software is crowded, but software purpose-built for road-to-rail modal shift (carbon-priced routing integrated with rail/intermodal capacity APIs) is nearly empty — most TMS tools optimize within trucking. A credible intermodal-shift engine pairing Class I capacity with shipper Scope 3 targets is an open seam.

variations.name: Hydrogen fuel cell buses & coaches
variations.description: Transit buses are hydrogen's strongest road niche because depot-based fueling solves the station problem and duty cycles favor fast refueling; European fuel-cell bus registrations grew ~163% in 2025 even as truck players collapsed.

companies.name: Solaris Bus & Coach
companies.what: European fuel-cell bus market leader (Urbino hydrogen family), owned by Spain's CAF Group
companies.signal: Delivered 306 hydrogen buses in 2025 for a 58% European FC-bus share; €1.18B revenue 2025

companies.name: Wrightbus
companies.what: Northern Irish maker of the world's first hydrogen double-decker and Kite Hydroliner single-deckers, expanding fast in Germany
companies.signal: 1,200+ buses produced in 2025 (+20% YoY); ~130 hydrogen buses on German roads by end-2025 (Saarbahn 28, Cottbus 46, WestVerkehr 12)

companies.name: Van Hool
companies.what: Belgian bus/coach maker that was an early fuel-cell bus pioneer in Europe and the US
companies.signal: Declared bankrupt April 2024; bus activities taken over by VDL/Schmitz Cargobull; De Lijn retired its Van Hool H2 buses and dismantled the Antwerp H2 station

companies.name: CaetanoBus
companies.what: Portuguese builder (Toyota/Mitsui-backed) of the H2.City Gold fuel-cell bus using Toyota stacks
companies.signal: Fuel-cell bus fleets delivered across Spain, Portugal, Germany and UK

companies.name: New Flyer (NFI Group)
companies.what: North America's largest transit bus maker, building Xcelsior CHARGE FC hydrogen buses
companies.signal: Selected Hexagon Purus hydrogen tanks for the fifth consecutive year; growing US FC bus orders under FTA Low-No grants

variations.name: Hydrogen passenger cars (light-duty FCEVs)
variations.description: Fuel-cell sedans and SUVs refuel in minutes with zero tailpipe emissions, but collapsing station networks and $30+/kg retail hydrogen have shrunk the market to a few OEM flagships and fleet niches, making this a contrarian bet on future infrastructure.

companies.name: Toyota
companies.what: Mirai, the highest-volume FCEV car ever, plus third-generation fuel-cell systems licensed to other OEMs
companies.signal: Mirai sales slumped with California's station closures, but Toyota continues FC development and supplies BMW's 2028 program

companies.name: Hyundai Motor
companies.what: Nexo FCEV SUV, refreshed with a new generation launched 2025 (from the Initium concept)
companies.signal: One of only two FCEV cars in series production globally; Korea remains the largest FCEV car market

companies.name: Honda
companies.what: CR-V e:FCEV, a US-built plug-in hybrid fuel-cell SUV using a co-developed GM fuel-cell system
companies.signal: Low-volume lease program in California; keeps Honda's FC supply chain alive for trucks/stationary

companies.name: BMW
companies.what: iX5 Hydrogen pilot fleet, with the brand's first series-production FCEV due 2028 using Toyota's gen-3 stack
companies.signal: 1M+ km of pilot-fleet testing complete; 2028 series launch confirmed for Germany/France first

companies.name: Riversimple
companies.what: Welsh maker of the ultra-light two-seat Rasa FCEV offered only via all-inclusive subscription (insurance, fuel, servicing bundled)
companies.signal: Beta testing in Abergavenny with subscription launch announced August 2025 — still pre-commercial after 20+ years

companies.name: HysetCo
companies.what: Paris operator of Europe's largest hydrogen taxi fleet (Hype legacy) with its own urban refueling stations — the fleet-plus-depot model that makes FCEV cars pencil
companies.signal: Raised ~€200M in 2024 led by Hy24 to scale Paris-region fleet and stations

companies.name: Hopium
companies.what: French startup that abandoned its Machina hydrogen sedan after near-collapse and pivoted to selling fuel-cell stacks
companies.signal: Went through judicial reorganization in 2023; survival as a component supplier unproven

variations.white_space: Retail FCEV cars are in retreat — Shell closed all California light-duty stations in 2024 and Mirai resale values cratered — because chicken-and-egg station economics fail at low vehicle density. The viable opening is captive fleets with depot fueling (taxis, government fleets) as HysetCo demonstrates, not retail.
